implementation_notes: JavaScript has no queue in the standard library and cannot share node objects between agents, so the only honest realization of the classic structure is a bounded index ring over a SharedArrayBuffer whose control words are read and published with Atomics: load or compare-exchange the head/tail tickets, write the payload, then publish with a release store. Waiting uses Atomics.wait/notify, which throws on the main thread, so producers and consumers must be workers (or use Atomics.waitAsync); message passing with postMessage/MessageChannel is the idiomatic substitute and needs no shared memory at all. Keep the ring for traffic that must bypass the event loop - inside one thread JavaScript is already serialised, so a lock-free queue there is pure overhead.
pitfalls: Atomics.wait throws on the main thread, and SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation in browsers - verify crossOriginIsolated or the ring silently has no shared memory.
Typed arrays hold numbers only: objects cannot be shared by reference, so either copy them through postMessage or store indices into a per-agent table.
The event loop already serialises ordinary JavaScript; a queue is only worth its complexity across workers, never within one thread.
